expected_findings.expected_claim: The February prescribing record discontinued lisinopril and ordered losartan, but later emergency and primary-care records retain or report lisinopril exposure with uncertain timing; the records establish a documentation discrepancy, not confirmed ingestion.

anchors.quote: Lisinopril 20 mg tablet is discontinued in the electronic order list
Discharge medication list imported from an outside pharmacy includes lisinopril 20 mg daily
Patient brought an old bottle labeled lisinopril 20 mg

expected_findings.counterevidence: The patient could not confirm the last dose, and no administration or dispensing record proves ingestion.

expected_findings.expected_claim: Creatinine rose from 1.18 mg/dL at baseline to 1.68 mg/dL during the diarrheal illness, then partially improved to 1.27 mg/dL; potassium was transiently elevated and later normalized.
expected_findings.counterevidence: The renal trend overlaps with poor intake, diarrhea, and reported NSAID exposure; causation is not established.

expected_non_findings.reason: Specialist documentation lists multiple plausible contributors and explicitly preserves uncertainty.
Patient report and an old bottle indicate possible exposure but do not prove ingestion dates.

evaluation_criteria: Verify the structured renal laboratory trend.
Separate order, reconciliation, patient report, and ingestion.
Represent volume depletion and NSAID exposure as competing contributors.
Cite source IDs and preserve uncertainty.
acceptable_uncertainty: The exact last lisinopril dose is unknown.
Dispensing and administration are not available.
Causality between any medicine and renal change is unproven.
clinical_review: Synthetic data consistency review only; no independent medical expert validation was performed.
